From 665e985c2f41bebc3e6cee7e04c36a44afbc58f7 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Joe Perches <joe@perches.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jul 2019 22:04:19 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] mmc: meson-mx-sdio: Fix misuse of GENMASK macro

Arguments are supposed to be ordered high then low.

Signed-off-by: Joe Perches <joe@perches.com>
Reviewed-by: Neil Armstrong <narmstrong@baylibre.com>
Fixes: ed80a13bb4c4 ("mmc: meson-mx-sdio: Add a driver for the Amlogic
Meson8 and Meson8b SoCs")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Ulf Hansson <ulf.hansson@linaro.org>

diff --git a/drivers/mmc/host/meson-mx-sdio.c b/drivers/mmc/host/meson-mx-sdio.c
index 2d736e416775..ba9a63db73da 100644
--- a/drivers/mmc/host/meson-mx-sdio.c
+++ b/drivers/mmc/host/meson-mx-sdio.c
@@ -73,7 +73,7 @@
 	#define MESON_MX_SDIO_IRQC_IF_CONFIG_MASK		GENMASK(7, 6)
 	#define MESON_MX_SDIO_IRQC_FORCE_DATA_CLK		BIT(8)
 	#define MESON_MX_SDIO_IRQC_FORCE_DATA_CMD		BIT(9)
-	#define MESON_MX_SDIO_IRQC_FORCE_DATA_DAT_MASK		GENMASK(10, 13)
+	#define MESON_MX_SDIO_IRQC_FORCE_DATA_DAT_MASK		GENMASK(13, 10)
 	#define MESON_MX_SDIO_IRQC_SOFT_RESET			BIT(15)
 	#define MESON_MX_SDIO_IRQC_FORCE_HALT			BIT(30)
 	#define MESON_MX_SDIO_IRQC_HALT_HOLE			BIT(31)
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/mmc/host/meson-mx-sdio.c`**
- The macro definition for `MESON_MX_SDIO_IRQC_FORCE_DATA_DAT_MASK` was modified. 
- The original line:
  ```c
  #define MESON_MX_SDIO_IRQC_FORCE_DATA_DAT_MASK		GENMASK(10, 13)
  ```
  was changed to:
  ```c
  #define MESON_MX_SDIO_IRQC_FORCE_DATA_DAT_MASK		GENMASK(13, 10)
  ```
- This change corrects the order of the arguments passed to the `GENMASK` macro, ensuring that the high value (13) is specified before the low value (10).

### Relationships
- The modification in `meson-mx-sdio.c` addresses a misuse of the `GENMASK` macro, which is crucial for defining bit masks correctly. 
- The patch is linked to a previous commit (ed80a13bb4c4) that introduced the driver for Amlogic Meson8 and Meson8b SoCs, indicating that this bug fix is part of ongoing maintenance and improvement of that driver. 
- The change is also marked for stable inclusion, suggesting its importance in ensuring the reliability of the driver in production environments.

Here is the commit message:
mmc: meson-mx-sdio: Fix misuse of GENMASK macro

Arguments are supposed to be ordered high then low.

Signed-off-by: Joe Perches <joe@perches.com>
Reviewed-by: Neil Armstrong <narmstrong@baylibre.com>
Fixes: ed80a13bb4c4 ("mmc: meson-mx-sdio: Add a driver for the Amlogic
Meson8 and Meson8b SoCs")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Ulf Hansson <ulf.hansson@linaro.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the incorrect ordering of arguments in the `GENMASK` macro, where the low value (10) was specified before the high value (13). This misuse can lead to incorrect bitmask definitions, potentially causing unintended behavior in the driver that relies on these masks for configuring hardware registers.

Here is the patch:
 	#define MESON_MX_SDIO_IRQC_FORCE_DATA_CLK		BIT(8)
 	#define MESON_MX_SDIO_IRQC_FORCE_DATA_CMD		BIT(9)
-	#define MESON_MX_SDIO_IRQC_FORCE_DATA_DAT_MASK		GENMASK(10, 13)
+	#define MESON_MX_SDIO_IRQC_FORCE_DATA_DAT_MASK		GENMASK(13, 10)
 	#define MESON_MX_SDIO_IRQC_SOFT_RESET			BIT(15)
 	#define MESON_MX_SDIO_IRQC_FORCE_HALT			BIT(30)

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
#define MESON_MX_SDIO_IRQC_FORCE_DATA_DAT_MASK		GENMASK(10, 13)
```
Reason:
The `GENMASK` macro was incorrectly called with the low value (10) before the high value (13), which results in an incorrect bitmask definition. This can lead to unintended behavior in the driver that relies on this mask for configuring hardware registers, as the generated mask will not cover the intended bits.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
#define MESON_MX_SDIO_IRQC_FORCE_DATA_DAT_MASK		GENMASK(13, 10)
```
Reason:
The patch corrects the argument order in the `GENMASK` macro by placing the high value (13) before the low value (10). This ensures that the bitmask is defined correctly, covering the intended bits and preventing any unintended behavior in the driver.
